clue.text: Dandy in a vehicle on entering M1

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the preceding words go within the letters of the motorway name

parts.note: the M of the motorway and the digit 1 written as the Roman numeral I
taken as written
a car is a vehicle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dapper man is riding in a car as it joins the M1 motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; its name splits into the letter M and the digit 1 as a Roman numeral, which go either side of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: In eighteenth-century Britain a macaroni was a fashionable young man affecting continental dress, the sense in Yankee Doodle.

parts.note: surface reading: buying the next set of drinks at the pub
setter's reading: putting fresh ammunition into a gun

explanation.walkthrough: A round is both a set of drinks bought for a group and a single shot of ammunition; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Charging a firearm again inserts another cartridge, so the next shot is ready to fire.

indicators.note: something done terribly is badly messed up, so the preceding letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the eight letters of both words

explanation.surface: Someone's pride and so on have taken a terrible beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something worn out and in poor condition from age or rough use.

indicators.note: a head wearing headgear sits inside it, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: a beret is a kind of soft cap
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A man is sweating in his beret.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is an informal British word for a man, just as fellow is.

indicators.note: reversed tells us the joined pieces are to be read from back to front

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a memo
to dart is to move suddenly

explanation.surface: A vessel under way abruptly goes astern.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader is a merchant vessel, a ship that carries goods for commerce.

parts.note: surface reading: a comedian from France
setter's reading: one particular person surnamed French, the British comedian of French and Saunders

explanation.walkthrough: The comic actress of French and Saunders and The Vicar of Dibley is a well-known British comedian; the answer is her first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue asks for the given name of the comedian whose surname is French, which is also the word for daybreak.

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: taken as written
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: Spectators spot a former Wimbledon winner in the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Virginia Wade won the women's singles at Wimbledon in 1977, the last British woman to do so for decades.
explanation.definitionFit: The British tennis player Virginia Wade took the Wimbledon ladies' singles title in 1977.

clue.text: Heavenly tale wrong about this place

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters wrap the other piece
a word put wrong is in the incorrect order, so its letters need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
here means in this place

explanation.surface: A story about a celestial location has been got wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal describes something airy and unearthly, of the sky or the spirit world, as heavenly does.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the twelve feats Hercules had to perform
second meaning: the British political party in government

explanation.surface: A huge job awaits the party in power.
explanation.walkthrough: Hercules performed twelve tasks known as his Labours; the Labour Party is one of Britain's two main parties and currently governs.
explanation.definitionFit: The myth calls each of Hercules' feats a labour, and Labour is also the name of the UK party now in office.

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the rearranged letters receive another piece
something corrected is altered and put into a different form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A skilled person, having been put right, greets a newcomer who insists on the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant fusses over tiny rules and details, exactly the habit of someone called a stickler.

parts.note: prim means prudish or stiffly proper
Rose is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A prim woman commits an embarrassing blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a British word for a blunder, which the surface uses; here it means a flower, something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring flower, and a bloomer is a punning crossword name for any flowering plant.

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about in disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bother someone who is even more irritable once intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: Rattier is British slang for crosser or more bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: To irritate someone is to get on their nerves, the same as to annoy them.

indicators.note: outside places the first piece around the second, which sits within it

parts.note: a sister is a relative
in means at home

explanation.surface: A threatening family member is lurking outside the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister describes something threatening or suggesting harm, which is what menacing also means.

indicators.note: something reported is spoken out, so we go by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: Dick is a familiar form of Richard
murphy and tater are both slang for a potato

explanation.surface: A man named Richard Murphy is said to be a despot.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy is a slang word for a potato, from its association with Ireland, and tater is another.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictator rules alone with absolute power, often cruelly, which is what a tyrant does.

indicators.note: something faulty is not working properly, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A broken television set sits close to the pub counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is an inn or public house serving drink, and a bar is such a place.

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hour
and means with or plus

explanation.surface: Sixty minutes in the company of a group called the Banana Bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make Banana Bunch look like a name, perhaps a band or children's show; read lower case it is just a cluster of bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: Grocers call a cluster of bananas growing together on the stalk a hand, each fruit being a finger.

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of the name
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: The leading Henley rowing crew are being sized up.
explanation.walkthrough: Henley-on-Thames hosts Britain's famous summer rowing regatta, which suits the crew of eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Height is the vertical measurement of something, how far it goes upward from the ground.

clue.text: English in British state work hard

indicators.note: in places this piece within the letters of the following ones

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
E is the abbreviation for English
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: An Englishman in a British country toils away.
explanation.definitionFit: To beaver away is an idiom for working busily and steadily, like the industrious animal.

clue.text: Two lines penned by each girl

indicators.note: something penned is shut in an enclosure, so this piece sits inside the next

parts.note: EA is the abbreviation for each
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled

explanation.surface: Each girl writes a couple of lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a girl's name, and crosswords often define a first name simply by sex.

parts.note: to rig is to fix dishonestly, as with a match
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rearrange something for a city in Latvia.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga is the capital and largest urban centre of Latvia on the Baltic.

clue.text: Artist Damien on time to show desire

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
Damien Hirst is the British artist known for the pickled shark

explanation.surface: Damien Hirst turns up punctually to display his ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, A on B puts A after B, so the artist follows the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirst is used figuratively for a strong craving, as in a thirst for knowledge.

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: everything on the other side, nothing on the left
second meaning: an interjection of acceptance, like OK

explanation.walkthrough: None left is a whimsical description: if nothing is left, every item is on the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works as a cheerful interjection meaning OK, and literally says every item sits to the starboard side.

indicators.note: radio is heard not seen, so we go by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: he would is contracted to he'd

explanation.surface: A broadcaster says a man would pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed is to pay attention to advice, which is what listening means here.
